newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Laverton plans Continental Gold merge.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Laverton plans Continental Gold merge.

text.p: Laverton Gold NL said on Monday it planned to merge with Continental Goldfields Ltd to create a single company with immediate attributable gold production of 130,000 ounces a year.

Under the proposed merger, Laverton said it would offer four of its shares for every five Continental shares and four new options for every five existing Continental options. The new options would be exerciseable at 50 cents on or before December 31, 1998

Laverton shares closed on Friday at 32 cents while Continental fetched 26 cents. Trading in both companies was halted by the Australian Stock Exchange on Monday pending announcement of the merger plans.
Laverton is developing the Rawas gold and silver deposit in southern Sumatra, Indonesia, while Continental treats mine waste in South Africa.

Following the merger, Continental planned to shift part of its exploration focus to Western Australia, where Laverton holds a 10 percent interest in the grass roots Mt Celia gold prospect. It is also earning a 75 percent interest in the Irwin Hills
nickel and platinum project in Western Australia.
Laverton said the merged companies would have a combined capitalisation of about A$60 million and would probably seek a listing on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.

The Rawas project was commissioned last January and is projected to produce about 75,000 ounces a year. Production from the mine is hedged for the next 18 months at an average price of US$406 an ounce, Laverton said.
The deposit contains 1.140 million ounces of gold and gold equivalent, Laverton said.

The strategy of the merged company, to be called Transcontinental Resources, would be to expand production to 300,000 ounces a year as quickly as possible by funding exploration in Indonesia and expanding production in South Africa.
It would also seek to acquire gold producing assets in Australia, the company added.
Continental last year acquired as 24.3 percent stake in Knights Gold Mining Co Ltd for shares valued at A$7.22 million.
Knights produces 50,000 ounces of gold annually, primarily from the retreatment of tailings dumps located near Johannesburg.
The South African miner has reserves of 84 million tonnes of retreatable material within its dumps equating to 1.4 million ounces of contained gold, Continental figures show.
Knights owns and operates a processing plant with a capacity in excess of three million tonnes per annum.
Economic mine-life of the present dumps at current extraction rates is in excess of 13 years, Continental has said.

"Strategically, it is expected that Transcontinental will be absorbed by a new Canadian company, which will apply for listing on the Toronto Stock Exchange and which will seek a sub-listing on the Australian Stock Exchange," Laverton said.
